title: The place
subtitle: Austria's warm east
objectives: Explain the role of Lake Neusiedl

steps.title: On the Hungarian border
steps.body: Burgenland is Austria's easternmost state, a long strip along the Hungarian border, south-east of Vienna. It belonged to Hungary until 1921. It has about 11,700 hectares of vines. Key areas include Neusiedlersee, around the lake; Leithaberg, on the hills to the west; Mittelburgenland; and Eisenberg in the south.

steps.title: Pannonian climate
steps.body: Burgenland has a warm, dry Pannonian climate, influenced by the Hungarian plain: hot summers, cold winters and plenty of sun. It's Austria's warmest wine region, which is why it's the country's red wine heartland. Soils vary: limestone and schist on the Leithaberg, clay in Mittelburgenland, gravel and sand by the lake.

steps.prompt: Why is Burgenland Austria's red wine heartland?
options: Its warm Pannonian climate ripens red grapes
steps.explanation: Warmth from the Hungarian plain helps reds ripen.

steps.title: Lake Neusiedl
steps.body: Lake Neusiedl, Neusiedlersee, is a large, shallow steppe lake, about 320 km2 but only about 1 to 2 m deep, on the border with Hungary. It warms the area and, in autumn, creates mist and humidity that favour noble rot. The lake and its reed beds are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a national park.

steps.explanation: Not true. It's large but only about 1 to 2 m deep.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Burgenland is Austria's warm east, part of Hungary until 1921
Its Pannonian climate makes it Austria's red heartland
Shallow Lake Neusiedl brings warmth and autumn mist
